subject: Medvera packaging inquiry: consolidation, downgrade credits, and observability trial
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medvera.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Package consolidation and question about downgrade credits

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for taking a look. We ran into a packaging question while prepping our Q1 budget: we currently plan to reduce committed seats by ~25% in January if usage doesn't climb as expected. A few specific asks:

- If we consolidate to a Compact bundle (smaller base but feature add-ons), can unused committed seats be converted into credit for future bursts or addons? If so, how does that conversion look (timing, caps, expiry)?
- Alternatively, if we stay on Core and toggle modular feature add-ons, what pricing delta should we expect on observability and deduplication features?
- Is there a standard cadence for stepdown credits (e.g., a 30/60/90 day grace ladder) when customers reduce committed throughput?

I've attached our usage requirements and projected seat plan (Medvera_Requirements.xlsx) so you can see the numbers.

Can you point us to the standard options and — if possible — a quick sketch of two concession paths so we can evaluate with procurement? If it's easier to talk, we can do a 30-minute sync this week.

Elena Torres
Director of ML Ops
Medvera

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medvera.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Package consolidation and question about downgrade credits

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the details and the attachment — this is exactly the right level of context. I pulled a quick sketch together and uploaded an initial bundle comparison to Drive (link below). High level guidance up front:

Option A — Consolidated Compact
- Lower base commit, features bundled as paid addons
- Good if you expect inconsistent usage and want predictable smaller baseline spend
- Downgrade path: we can convert unused committed seats to platform credit at a negotiated rate (see Ben's note soon) with a 12-month expiry typical; cap often sits between 15–25% of committed value depending on term length

Option B — Core + Modular
- Higher base, more features included; individual add-ons toggled on/off
- Better for steady throughput and when observability/retention are required long-term
- Stepdown credits usually more conservative because commitment is larger; conversion windows shorter (90 days typical)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Ben will propose a concrete "grace ladder" and a credit cap example you can show procurement.
2) If you prefer Compact, we'll paper a pilot amendment that preserves add-on trial access for 30 days after downsize.
3) If procurement wants a blanket PO, share the template and we'll attach a Draft AMS/PO.

Quick questions for procurement when you loop them in: do they require firm dollar-for-dollar crediting vs. percentage-of-commit credits? Also, is observability retention a must-have or a trial requirement?

Drive sketch: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aMedveraBundleSketch
HubSpot record: hubspot:contacts:123456789

Talk soon — happy to set up a call.

Naomi Feldman

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medvera.com>, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2025-11-03T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Package consolidation and question about downgrade credits

Elena / Naomi —

Thanks for the clear ask. Below are two pragmatic structures we commonly offer for stepdowns; I marked tradeoffs so you can evaluate with procurement.

Structure 1 — Grace Ladder (recommended for Compact moves)
- Day 0–30 after contract change: 100% conversion of unused committed seats into platform credit (applied to token/throughput charges)
- Day 31–90: 50% conversion rate
- After Day 90: credit conversion allowed but pro-rated at monthly realized usage rate
- Credit expiry: 12 months from issuance
- Cap: credits may not exceed 20% of the originally committed annual value without executive approval

Structure 2 — Conservative Conversion (recommended for Core customers)
- Single-tier conversion window: 60 days at 60% conversion rate
- Credit expiry: 6–9 months depending on term
- Cap: 10–15% of committed annual value

Two commercial offers to present to procurement:
A) Consolidated Compact proposal — lower baseline commit; observability and advanced dedupe as paid addons (we can include a 30-day trial for retention addon after a downsize)
B) Core with toggles — higher baseline; addons priced lower but fewer conversion concessions on stepdown

I attached a draft blanket PO language to show how credits are reflected in an AMS amendment (Draft_AMS_Blanket_PO.pdf). If Medvera prefers A, we can propose an initial 6-month Compact pilot with a 20% credit cap and the Grace Ladder structure above.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with Priyom (pricing lead) and Lauren (product) to finalize numbers. What times work for you this week?

—Ben

Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful and much clearer. Medvera's procurement prefers the Consolidated Compact model (Option A) but needs explicit numbers for the Grace Ladder to circulate.

Two quick asks before we set the PO in motion:
1) Can you confirm the exact conversion formula you would apply to unused seat dollars (example: $X unused -> $Y credit) under the Day 0–30 and Day 31–90 bands? A simple percentage example by seat would be perfect.
2) We want to trial observability retention for 30 days post-downgrade; is that covered under the Compact pilot as Ben suggested?

If you can provide the sample numbers I can get procurement moving; cc'd procurement@medvera.com for visibility. If it's easier, set a 30-minute slot and we'll take it live.

Regards,
Elena
